## Windows PowerShell 7 and T3 process integration

Windows Grokgod now requires PowerShell 7 or newer. Install PowerShell 7 before updating; the installer provides an explicit `-InstallPowerShell7` setup helper, and `-Apply` opts into running the documented installation command. A Windows PowerShell 5.1 entry may only relaunch the installer under verified PowerShell 7 or print prerequisite guidance.

- Grokgod launchers, updater and background refresh select a verified PowerShell 7 engine without a Windows PowerShell 5.1 fallback.
- Version, help, model inspection and agent-stdio launches bypass wrapper update notices and background network refreshes.
- Status and installer version probes drain output concurrently, enforce deadlines and clean up only processes they own.
- Generated Windows launchers have native regression coverage for redirected stdin/stdout/stderr, EOF, protocol initialization, argument forwarding and exit codes.
- Windows/T3 setup documentation explains direct patched-binary selection, `GROK_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, and the difference between the Grokgod release and bundled engine versions.

The original MSI-1 T3 timeout trigger remains unproven. The direct patched-binary configuration is the documented mitigation; the process fixes in this release are independently verified defects and are not claimed as that incident's root cause.

The pinned Grok engine and numbered patch stack are unchanged by this release.
